HOOK
They cut the tails off rats, then let every single one go.
SETUP
Why would anyone do that? In 1902, Hanoi was crawling with rats, and its French rulers were terrified of the plague.
PLAN
So they hired rat catchers and paid them for every rat they killed.
BUT
But counting dead rats was a mess, so the French changed the rule: just bring us the tail.
THEN
Then they opened the offer to everyone in the city: one cent for every rat tail.
CONFLICT
Within weeks, officials noticed something strange. Rats were running around with no tails.
PIVOT
You see, the reward was for the tail, not the rat. So a rat that stayed alive and kept breeding was worth far more than a dead one.
ESCALATION
People cut off the tails and set the rats free. Some even started raising rats, just to harvest more tails.
SO
So the French paid for more and more tails, while the rats multiplied. In the end, they cancelled the whole program.
PAYOFF
Economists call this a perverse incentive: pay people for the measurement, and they will give you the measurement, not the result.
CLOSE
The French wanted fewer rats. They paid for tails, and that is exactly what they got.
